_comment: Outlets the Scraper reads, as data so adding one is a config edit.
Feed URLs only — the Scraper does not crawl article pages (issue #1,
story 21: respect robots.txt and rate limits). Issue #1 names FMT, Malay
Mail, NST, The Star, The Vibes, Sinar Daily and Bernama; only outlets
whose feed has been verified to work are listed here.
Two of the seven are absent, each for its own reason (issue #11).
Re-check before assuming either is still true:
- The Star: no working feed. Its own RSS directory page at
/news/nation/rss advertises ~30 feeds, and every one of them returns
404 — the directory is stale, not our request. Verified not to be
user-agent dependent: a browser user agent gets the same 404.
- Sinar Daily: robots.txt disallows /rss and /rssFeed/* for every user
agent but Facebook's. Story 21 says we respect that, so there is
nothing to do here unless they change the rules.
Berita Harian and Utusan Malaysia are read in Bahasa Malaysia (issue #1,
story 22, by way of issue #13), and are the two outlets here that story 9
does not name. Of the seven it does, only Bernama has a Malay edition,
and /bm/rssfeed.php — the one URL Bernama's own Malay site advertises —
still answers 500 with an empty body, re-checked 6 Aug 2026. Its English
feed below is unaffected.
The pair is two publishers on purpose. Berita Harian is NSTP's Malay
daily and Utusan Malaysia is a separate newsroom with a different
political lean, so the Malay half of the sample is not one editorial
line. Harian Metro was verified working too and deliberately left out:
it is NSTP's third feed after Berita Harian and NST, it syndicates the
same political copy as Berita Harian nearly verbatim, and Sentiment is
an unweighted mean over articles — so adding it would weight one
newsroom three times rather than widen the sample.
Utusan's robots.txt disallows only /wp-admin/ and is read normally.
Berita Harian is listed here but is not currently being read. Its
robots.txt allowed every user agent at the feed path when it was added
on 6 August 2026, and on 8 August began answering 403 — which the
Scraper treats as a refusal, so the outlet is skipped. The refusal is
not user-agent dependent: this project's agent, a browser agent and
plain curl all get 403, repeatably. The feed itself still answers 200;
only robots.txt is blocked, which reads like CDN bot protection rather
than a decision about us.
It is kept here rather than removed because the entry costs one skipped
request a day and the block may lift as quickly as it appeared. Re-check
with:  curl -sI https://www.bharian.com.my/robots.txt
A 200 means it is being read again, and the run output says so either
way (issue #16). If this is still 403 by, say, November 2026, drop it
and find another Malay outlet — Utusan alone carries about ten items.
Bernama dates no item in its feed, so its Articles carry no
published_at. Why that is kept rather than guessed at is on the field
itself, in domain.py.
